description: Labelled answers to three fresh-set questions, written from the fixture code by an agent that did not see the grader's rules (2026-11-12). Synthetic.

answers.answer: A loan can be renewed at most 2 times, and each renewal adds 14 days to the due date.
MAX_RENEWALS is 2 and RENEWAL_DAYS is 14, so a member can renew twice, gaining 14 extra days each time.
Up to two renewals are allowed. Every successful renew() call pushes dueAt forward by RENEWAL_DAYS * DAY_MS, which is 14 days.
Two renewals, 14 days each. A third attempt throws 'No renewals left.'
According to settings.js, MAX_RENEWALS = 2 and RENEWAL_DAYS = 14. In loans.js, renew() refuses once loan.renewals reaches 2, and otherwise adds 14 days to dueAt and increments the counter.
Each loan can be extended twice. Each extension is two weeks (14 days), so with the initial 21-day loan the longest possible loan is 49 days.
The limit is 2 renewals per loan. Each one adds 14 days.
A borrower may renew a loan a maximum of two times; each renewal extends the due date by 14 days from the current due date, not from today.

renew() checks loan.renewals >= MAX_RENEWALS (2) and throws if the limit is hit. Otherwise it does loan.dueAt += RENEWAL_DAYS * DAY_MS, i.e. 14 days, and bumps loan.renewals by one. So: two renewals of 14 days.
You get 2 renewals. Each renewal gives you another 14 days.
The code caps renewals at two (MAX_RENEWALS) and each renewal is worth fourteen days (RENEWAL_DAYS). The renewal is also refused if someone else has a hold on the item.

Loans start with renewals: 0. Each renewal increments that and adds 14 days, until renewals reaches 2, after which renew() throws an error. So twice, 14 days per renewal, for a maximum of 28 extra days.
Short answer: twice, and each renewal adds two weeks to the due date.
The due date can be extended by 14 days on each renewal, and a loan can be renewed no more than 2 times.
Based on the constants, a loan may be renewed up to 2 times. Each renewal moves dueAt 14 days later. Once the second renewal has been used, further attempts fail with 'No renewals left.'
A loan can be renewed up to 3 times, and each renewal adds 14 days.
Each loan can be renewed twice, and each renewal adds 21 days, the same as the original loan period.
MAX_RENEWALS is 2 and each renewal resets the due date to 14 days from the day of the renewal.
There is no limit on renewals in the code; each renewal adds RENEWAL_DAYS, which is 14 days.
A loan can be renewed once, for an extra 14 days.
Loans can be renewed 2 times, adding 7 days each time.
Each renewal adds 14 days.
You can renew a loan twice. Each renewal extends the loan by 14 days, but a renewal fee is charged through fees.js for every renewal after the first.
The member can renew up to MAX_ACTIVE_LOANS times, which is 8, and each renewal is 14 days.
A loan may be renewed up to two times. Renewals are handled by the reminder queue, which sends a reminder 3 days before the due date and renews the loan automatically for another 14 days.
Renewals are capped at 2, and each one adds a full loan period of LOAN_DAYS (21 days) to the due date.
Loans can be renewed as many times as the member likes as long as nobody has placed a hold. Each renewal adds 14 days.
Members can renew a loan 2 times.
The code allows 4 renewals of 14 days each, for a total of 56 extra days.
Each loan can be renewed twice, for 14 days the first time and 7 days the second time.
The renewal is refused. renew() throws 'Item is on hold for another member.' and the due date is not changed.

renew() calls hasHoldFor(loan.itemId, loan.memberId). If another member has a non-expired hold, it throws an Error with the message 'Item is on hold for another member.' before dueAt or renewals are touched, so the loan is not extended.
It fails. The member gets the error 'Item is on hold for another member.' and keeps the original due date; the renewal count does not go up either.
The member cannot renew. Because someone else is waiting for the item, renew() throws an error and the loan stays as it was.
If any other member holds the item (and that hold has not expired), the renewal is blocked with an exception: 'Item is on hold for another member.' Nothing about the loan is updated.
An error is thrown and the renewal does not happen. The check runs after the renewal-limit check, so if renewals remain, the hold check still stops it with 'Item is on hold for another member.'
The hold wins. renew() throws instead of extending the loan, so the member has to return the item by the existing due date.

Renewal is denied with 'Item is on hold for another member.' The loan's dueAt is left unchanged and loan.renewals is not incremented. A hold placed by the borrower themselves, or one that has expired, does not block renewal.
The code throws new Error('Item is on hold for another member.'), so the renewal is rejected and the loan is not extended.
They are blocked from renewing. hasHoldFor returns true when some hold on the item belongs to a different member and is not expired, and renew() then throws rather than adding RENEWAL_DAYS.
The renewal attempt raises an error saying the item is on hold for another member, and the loan keeps its current due date.
It's rejected: renew() throws before the line loan.dueAt += RENEWAL_DAYS * DAY_MS is reached, so no extra time is added.
When another member has an active hold, renewing is not allowed. The function throws 'Item is on hold for another member.' and the loan is not extended or counted as a renewal.
The member sees an 'Item is on hold for another member.' error and the loan is not renewed; the due date stays where it was.
renew() will throw. Renewal is only possible when no other member is waiting on (or has on the shelf) a hold for that item, so in this case the loan is not extended.
The renewal still goes through and the loan is extended by 14 days, but the member holding the item is moved to the front of the queue.
The loan is renewed, but only for half the normal period (7 days) because of the hold.
renew() throws 'No renewals left.' when there is a hold on the item.
The other member's hold is cancelled and the renewal succeeds, adding 14 days to the due date.
The renewal is accepted and a reminder is put on the harbor-reminders queue to tell the holding member that the item will be late.
The member is charged a late fee and the renewal is refused.
Holds do not affect renewals in this code. renew() only checks MAX_RENEWALS, so the loan is extended by 14 days.
The renewal is counted (loan.renewals goes up by one) but the due date is not extended because of the hold.
The renewal is queued and will be applied automatically if the hold expires before the due date.
The member is blocked from borrowing until the item is returned, and their renewal is processed after the other member picks up the item.
renew() succeeds, but the loan is marked so that it cannot be renewed again while the hold is active.
The code checks for holds with hasHoldFor.
The loan is renewed and the item is placed on the hold shelf for the other member as soon as the renewed loan is returned, with a 5-day pickup window.
An error is shown only if the hold belongs to the same member; if another member has a hold, the renewal goes ahead normally.
The renewal is allowed once even with a hold, but the second renewal will be rejected with 'Item is on hold for another member.'
When sweepShelf runs after the pickUpBy deadline, the hold's status is set to 'expired' and itemReturned is called again, so the next waiting hold is put on the shelf with a new 5-day pickup window.

The hold expires. The member had HOLD_SHELF_DAYS (5 days) to collect it; once that passes, sweepShelf marks the hold 'expired' and hands the item to the next member in the queue by calling itemReturned(itemId, now).
Their hold is marked expired and the item moves on to the next person waiting for it, who gets their own 5 days to pick it up.

sweepShelf loops over the item's holds; any hold that is 'on-shelf' with pickUpBy < now becomes 'expired', and then itemReturned is invoked, which finds the next hold with status 'waiting', sets it to 'on-shelf' and gives it pickUpBy = now + 5 days.
The missed hold expires and the item is offered to the next member in the hold queue.

If the item isn't picked up within 5 days, the hold is expired and the library passes the item to the next waiting hold. Because the hold is expired, it also no longer blocks the current borrower's renewals.
It gets expired by sweepShelf. The code then re-runs the return logic (itemReturned), so the next member whose hold is still 'waiting' is moved to 'on-shelf' and given a fresh pick-up deadline.
The hold lapses: its status changes from 'on-shelf' to 'expired'. The item then goes to whoever is next in line, as if it had just been returned.
After the 5-day hold shelf period ends, the uncollected hold is set to expired and the next waiting member's hold becomes active (on-shelf) with a new 5-day pickUpBy date.
The member loses the hold. sweepShelf flips it to 'expired' and calls itemReturned again, which passes the item to the next queued hold.

Holds on the shelf have a pickUpBy deadline of HOLD_SHELF_DAYS = 5 days. A sweep after that deadline expires the hold and calls itemReturned, so the item is handed to the next member waiting in the queue.
The hold is expired, and the item rolls over to the next waiting hold in the queue, which is placed on the hold shelf for that member.
In short: expired, then passed on. The no-show's hold status becomes 'expired', and calling itemReturned(itemId, now) promotes the next 'waiting' hold to 'on-shelf' with its own pick-up deadline.
When the pick-up window runs out, the hold is marked as expired and the next member waiting for the item gets it on the hold shelf; the expired member is skipped.
sweepShelf expires the overdue hold and immediately calls itemReturned, so the next member in the queue is offered the item with a new five-day window to collect it.
The hold expires and the item goes back on the regular shelf so anyone can borrow it.
When the 5 days are up, the hold is marked 'expired' and the item is returned to the general collection.
The member is charged a no-show fee and their hold is cancelled.
The hold is moved to the back of the queue with status 'waiting' so the member can try again later.
A reminder is sent through the harbor-reminders queue and the pick-up deadline is extended by another 5 days.
Nothing happens automatically; the hold stays on the shelf until a librarian removes it.
The hold expires after 7 days and the item is offered to the next member.
The hold is marked 'expired'.
sweepShelf deletes the hold from the queue and the item is put back into circulation as available.
The member is blocked from placing new holds until they pay the BLOCK_THRESHOLD_CENTS fee, and the item goes back to the shelf.
The hold is expired and the item is automatically checked out to the member who missed the pick-up, starting a 21-day loan.
The hold expires, and the item is returned to the member who originally borrowed it so they can renew it.
After HOLD_SHELF_DAYS the hold's status is reset to 'waiting' and itemReturned puts the same member's hold back on the shelf with a new deadline.
The hold simply lapses and the item becomes available for anyone to check out; the code does not look at the rest of the queue.
The member gets a late fee capped at LATE_FEE_CAP_CENTS and keeps the hold until the fee is paid.
